# Helper function to find Dropbox path

```{r find_dropbox}
get_dropbox_path <- function() {

  # Dropbox stores its configuration in info.json
  # This works for both personal and team Dropbox accounts

  if (.Platform$OS.type == "windows") {
    # On Windows, check both APPDATA and LOCALAPPDATA
    info_paths <- c(
      file.path(Sys.getenv("APPDATA"), "Dropbox", "info.json"),
      file.path(Sys.getenv("LOCALAPPDATA"), "Dropbox", "info.json")
    )
  } else {
    # On Mac/Linux
    info_paths <- file.path(Sys.getenv("HOME"), ".dropbox", "info.json")
  }

  # Find the first existing info.json
  info_path <- NULL
  for (p in info_paths) {
    if (file.exists(p)) {
      info_path <- p
      break
    }
  }

  if (is.null(info_path)) {
    stop("Could not find Dropbox info.json. Is Dropbox installed?")
  }

  # Read the JSON file
  info <- fromJSON(info_path)

  # Prefer business/team Dropbox if available, otherwise use personal
  if (!is.null(info$business)) {
    return(info$business$path)
  } else if (!is.null(info$personal)) {
    return(info$personal$path)
  } else {
    stop("Could not find Dropbox path in info.json")
  }
}

# Get the Dropbox path
dropbox_root <- get_dropbox_path()
message("Found Dropbox at: ", dropbox_root)
```

# Download NUTS1 data from BigQuery

```{r download_nuts1}
# Set your project ID
project_id <- "patbis"

# Specify dataset and table name
# Note: table is named nuts2 but actually contains NUTS1 codes (3 chars)
dataset <- "spatial"
table <- "docdb_nuts2_v3"

# Download the entire table
docdb_nuts1 <- bq_table_download(
  bq_table(project_id, dataset, table)
)

# Rename region_code to region_code for clarity (keeping consistent naming)
docdb_nuts1 <- docdb_nuts1 %>%
  rename(region_code = region_code)

# Preview the data
head(docdb_nuts1)
```

# Filter to keep only families in countrymap and get appln_id

```{r filter_countrymap}
# Read countrymap.fst from Dropbox to get the universe of valid docdb_family_ids and appln_ids
countrymap_path <- file.path(dropbox_root, "Apps", "iseapp", "countrymap.fst")
countrymap <- read_fst(countrymap_path)

# Create lookup for appln_id from countrymap
appln_id_lookup <- countrymap %>%
  select(docdb_family_id, appln_id) %>%
  distinct()

# Filter to keep only docdb_family_ids that exist in countrymap and join appln_id
n_before <- nrow(docdb_nuts1)

docdb_nuts1 <- docdb_nuts1 %>%
  inner_join(appln_id_lookup, by = "docdb_family_id")

n_after <- nrow(docdb_nuts1)

message("Filtered from ", n_before, " to ", n_after, " observations")
message("All rows now have appln_id: ", sum(!is.na(docdb_nuts1$appln_id)), " of ", nrow(docdb_nuts1))

# Show distinct regions after filtering
docdb_nuts1 %>%
  distinct(region_code) %>%
  arrange(region_code)
```

# Add region names

```{r add_region_names}
# UK NUTS1 region lookup table
# This can be expanded in the future to include other regions
region_names <- tibble::tribble(
  ~region_code, ~region_name,
  "UKC", "North East England",
  "UKD", "North West England",
  "UKE", "Yorkshire and The Humber",
  "UKF", "East Midlands",
  "UKG", "West Midlands",
  "UKH", "East of England",
  "UKI", "London",
  "UKJ", "South East England",
  "UKK", "South West England",
  "UKL", "Wales",
  "UKM", "Scotland",
  "UKN", "Northern Ireland"
)

# Join region names to the data
docdb_nuts1 <- docdb_nuts1 %>%
  left_join(region_names, by = "region_code")

# Preview
head(docdb_nuts1)

# Check for any unmatched codes
unmatched <- docdb_nuts1 %>%
  filter(is.na(region_name)) %>%
  distinct(region_code)

matched <- docdb_nuts1 %>%
  filter(!is.na(region_name)) %>%
  distinct(region_code)

if (nrow(unmatched) > 0) {
  warning("Unmatched region codes: ", paste(unmatched$region_code, collapse = ", "))
} else {
  message("All region codes matched to region names")
}

message("Matched region codes: ", paste(matched$region_code, collapse = ", "))

# Keep only matched codes
docdb_nuts1 <- docdb_nuts1 %>%
  filter(!is.na(region_name))
```

# Create regionmap (analogous to countrymap but for regions)

```{r create_regionmap}
# Create regionmap with the same structure as countrymap
# This allows the Region Explorer to work similarly to the Country Explorer
regionmap <- docdb_nuts1 %>%
  select(docdb_family_id, appln_id, region_code, region_name) %>%
  distinct()

message("Regionmap created with ", nrow(regionmap), " rows")
message("Regionmap columns: ", paste(names(regionmap), collapse = ", "))

# Summary by region
regionmap %>%
  group_by(region_code, region_name) %>%
  summarise(n_patents = n_distinct(docdb_family_id), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(desc(n_patents))
```

# Save regionmap to Dropbox

```{r save_regionmap}
# Define the output path in Dropbox Apps/iseapp folder
output_path <- file.path(dropbox_root, "Apps", "iseapp", "regionmap.fst")

# Create directory if it doesn't exist
dir.create(dirname(output_path), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# Write the data as fst file
write_fst(regionmap, output_path, compress = 100)

message("Regionmap saved to: ", output_path)
```
